key_insight: Tuning the flame-spraying O2/C2H2 ratio directly densifies Ni–Cr–B–Si self-fluxing coatings and improves their surface quality and adhesion.
engineering_relevance: Process-gas control is a practical lever for optimizing wear- and corrosion-resistant thermal-spray coatings on stainless-steel substrates.
method: Flame-sprayed Ni–Cr–B–Si coating onto AISI 321 steel with a Metal Coat 6PM-II system.
Varied O2/C2H2 ratio to 1.0, 1.1, and 1.2 while monitoring spray conditions with Accuraspray 4.0.
Measured microstructure, porosity, microhardness, roughness, and adhesion strength.
evidence_signal: As O2/C2H2 increased, porosity fell from 1.97±0.13% to 0.90±0.09%, roughness from 4.70±0.09 μm to 2.99±0.11 μm, and adhesion rose from 22.14±4.3 MPa to 35.02±3.9 MPa, with peak hardness of 1051.7 HV at 1.1.
watch_item: The best process window may depend on substrate, torch setup, and part geometry, so these settings should be revalidated before industrial transfer.
paper_title: EFFECT OF FLAME-SPRAYING TEMPERATURE ON THE PROPERTIES OF Ni–Cr–B–Si-BASED SELF-FLUXING COATINGS
